findings.source_quote: ἐμοῦ ἀναθεμένου μετὰ τὴν προσομιλίαν εὔξασθαι ὑπὲρ τῶν πασχόντων
findings.english_quote: when after the discourse I undertook to pray for those who were suffering
findings.issue: The draft makes the undertaking occur after the discourse without discussing the alternative sense of ἀναθεμένου as putting off or reserving the prayer. On that reading, μετὰ τὴν προσομιλίαν specifies the intended time of prayer, and the outcry occurs while that prayer is deferred. This materially affects the sequence and the force of the subsequent inability to endure even a short time. The supplied notes address neither the verb nor this temporal attachment.
findings.suggested_revision: Explicitly compare the current rendering with the candidate “when I had put off praying for those who were suffering until after the discourse.” Document the lexical sense and temporal attachment chosen, preserving the other viable reading in a source-quoted note. Any revised main wording requires fresh review; no correction of the verified Greek print is needed.

findings.source_quote: αὐτὰ τὰ πάθη τῇ πρὸς τὴν θρησκείαν τιμῇ ἀνέκραγεν
findings.english_quote: the afflictions themselves cried aloud out of respect for the religion
findings.issue: “Out of respect” favors the afflictions or their spiritual agents as the ones showing reverence. The causal dative also permits the outcry to be prompted by honor being paid to the religion, without identifying who pays that honor. The preceding reference to demons showing honor makes the draft defensible, but the alternative causal reading is material and is not disclosed by the existing note about personification.
findings.suggested_revision: Either retain the current wording with a note explaining the inferred source of the respect and preserving the alternative, or submit the less committal candidate “the afflictions themselves cried aloud because of the honor paid to the religion” for fresh review.
